input: is it possible to work on energy supply designs and efficient dense energy storage systems as a problem to work on long term... / I want this to be a direction that is worked on.
errors: Formula parser raised IndexError instead of ValueError on an unbalanced ')' (caught by its own test, fixed before commit)
WebFetch could not resolve osti.gov or webbook.nist.gov (DNS), so citations were checked with WebSearch only

doc_friction.issue: Adding a track touches five places (PROJECTS.md table and header count, pick_track.py PREFIX and constant, prompt-1.md 'thirteen tracks', projects.json theme, template.html colours); nothing lists them together.
Re-serialising with json.dumps reformats unrelated themes (the file has hand-placed ',{' separators); a new theme has to be spliced in as text to keep the diff small.
A parallel session added tracks 14 and 15 while this run was adding 'track 14'; the track number is a shared counter with no claim step, so the PR conflicted and the new track was renumbered to 16.

deviations.why: Routed with --track research because the owner named the task (a new long-term energy track); also edited research/PROJECTS.md to add the track, which the owner asked for directly.

Some inputs (Al-air, Li-O2, H2-O2 voltages; thermal and steel properties) could not be checked against a primary source in-session; labelled 'assumed' in the code and README rather than dropped, since the cross-checks against published totals still pass.

notes: New research track 16 (energy supply and dense storage) at the owner's request, plus milestone 1 research/energy-density: first-principles theoretical ceilings (Wh/kg) reproducing 5 published values within 0.3%, and the per-atom identity Wh/kg = 26,801 x eV/atom / g/mol.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a researcher deriving and cross-checking ~20 ceilings, writing tests, README and track plan

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
